lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Rebuilt the diagnostics service's monitoring dashboards around per-sensor error budgets, cutting mean time to detect incidents from 40 to 12 minutes.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.

- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue while rewriting the shared logging library, onboarding two new hires and taking over the weekend on-call rotation, which removed the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
- Raised diagnostic accuracy on 1,200 held-out cases from 71% to 79% by fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Cut p95 latency of single-request edge inference by 40% by serving the INT8 engine with dynamic batching.
- Using grouped tool-use rollouts, a composite reward over accuracy, citation validity and call count, and a GRPO loop with a frozen SFT reference, reduced end-to-end latency 5%.
- Stabilised GRPO training on sparse rewards by sampling a single rollout per prompt, so each update used exactly one scored trajectory.
- Documented the triage branch's abstention rules and escalation paths for the on-call reviewers, who adopted them as the team's runbook.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Cut p95 tool-call latency from 900 ms to 600 ms, a 50% reduction, by caching tool results and reusing completed sub-agent answers.
- Raised the runtime's task-completion rate by 12% on the benchmark suite, from 71% to 83%, by retrying failed sub-agent calls with their partial context.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Upstreamed 8 citation and faithfulness metrics to an open-source research-agent framework, where they now run in the default benchmark for every release.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Traced 3 structural pipeline defects in stability, sourcing and parameter handling to their modules with layered instrumentation; each was fixed upstream.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Make the code link go directly to your strongest relevant work.
items.because: A general profile may be less useful.

items.says: Add LinkedIn if it strengthens the application.
Consider relevant coursework when applying for internships.
items.because: It may fill a gap the experience section does not cover.

items.says: Use consistent date punctuation and location formatting across the education entries.
Move the Eastern Robotics role below the later Mobility Systems internship.
items.because: Experience should read in reverse chronological order.

items.says: Clarify how detection time was measured.
items.because: It would make the result more credible.

items.says: Clarify whether the dashboard change alone produced the reduction.
items.because: It would make the causal claim more credible.

items.says: Specify the load-test conditions if space permits.
items.because: p95 figures are more persuasive with a clear workload.

items.says: The bullet shifts from past to present tense.
State what the release cycle was before it became three days.
Split or narrow the overloaded bullet.
items.because: The migration, logging rewrite, onboarding, and on-call work compete for attention.

items.says: Clarify which change eliminated the nightly backlogs.
items.because: The reader cannot tell which change produced that result.

items.says: Define what counted as a pending case.
items.because: It would make the backlog comparison unambiguous.

items.says: Clarify whether the 68% drop was measured against the backlog at launch.
items.because: It would make the comparison unambiguous.

items.says: Identify the accuracy measure.
Explain what the 1,200 held-out cases represented.
Keep the training details only if target roles value them.
Single-request latency and dynamic batching appear technically at odds.
items.because: Batching generally depends on concurrent requests.

items.says: Explain the test conditions behind the latency measurement.
items.because: They would clarify the apparent conflict with dynamic batching.

items.says: Specify whether the 5% result is deployed inference latency or another end-to-end measure.
Explain how the training produced the latency change.
Shorten the methods description.
items.because: It takes more space than the result currently justifies.

items.says: One scored rollout per prompt appears inconsistent with standard GRPO.
items.because: Standard GRPO compares multiple rollouts within a prompt group.

items.says: State the actual grouping and update procedure.
Give a measurable indication of what ‘stabilised’ means.
Clarify whether you defined the abstention rules or documented agreed rules.
items.because: The distinction helps establish ownership beyond documentation.

items.says: Specify your scope if you owned a component rather than the entire suite.
items.because: ‘Owner’ is broad.

items.says: Substantiate the adoption, delivery-speed, and downstream-outcome claims or remove the bullet.
items.because: It is much less concrete than the other project bullets.

items.says: The stated 50% latency reduction is incorrect; 900 ms to 600 ms is a 33% reduction.
The increase from 71% to 83% is 12 percentage points, not an unqualified 12%.
Briefly identify the benchmark if it is not publicly recognizable.
Link to the upstream project or contributions if public.
items.because: ‘Contributor’ is more convincing when verifiable.

items.says: Specify whether you designed the metrics, implemented existing definitions, or both.
items.because: Those imply different levels of contribution.

items.says: Name what the evaluator scores were ranked against.
items.because: The 0.89 correlation needs a clear interpretation.

items.says: Clarify whether you fixed the defects or diagnosed them for others to fix.
items.because: ‘Fixed upstream’ leaves your role uncertain.

items.says: Git is listed under Programming but is a development tool, not a language.
Prioritize skills you can discuss in depth and tailor the line to each role.
Resolve the GRPO bullet before listing GRPO as a skill.
items.because: The bullet’s grouping and update procedure need to be checked.
